Frencken Group’s exposure to the AI boom comes through the complex components and modules it supplies to semiconductor equipment makers, which benefit from investment in chip production.

Its opportunities also extend to automotive radar antennas and gearbox solutions for humanoid and service robots, although the robotics business remains at an early stage.

Yields are based on closing prices on 29 October 2026 and distributions or dividends declared over the past 12 months.
A
high dividend yield
is easy to spot.
Working out what pays for it takes more work.
Mapletree Logistics Trust
(SGX: M44U), or MLT,
Genting Singapore
(SGX: G13) and
Frasers Logistics & Commercial Trust
(SGX: BUOU), or FLCT, all offer high yields at today’s prices.
Each one pays for its dividend in a different way, and that tells you more than the headline number.
Can MLT hold its DPU while it sells assets?
MLT owns 172 logistics properties across nine Asia-Pacific markets, with assets under management of S$13.1 billion as at 30 September 2026.
In the second quarter of its fiscal year ending 31 March 2027 (2QFY2027), MLT grew gross revenue 1.4% year on year (YoY) to S$180.0 million.
Net property income (NPI) edged up 1.0% to S$154.8 million.
Distribution per unit (DPU) was S$0.01816, up 0.1% YoY.
Several factors drove revenue higher: contributions from Mapletree Joo Koon Logistics Hub and an Indian acquisition, organic growth in Singapore, and a stronger renminbi and Australian dollar.
A weaker yen and lost income from divested properties partly offset these gains.
Higher property taxes pushed property expenses up 4.4% YoY.
Distributions to perpetual securities holders spiked 33.6% after MLT issued S$400 million of new perpetual securities ahead of redeeming an existing issue in November 2026.
Rental reversion improved to 2.1% from 0.9% in 1QFY2027, and was 4.2% excluding China.
China is the weak spot.
Portfolio occupancy was unchanged from the previous quarter at 96.4%.
MLT has divested about S$243 million of assets so far in FY2027 at an average 3.1% premium to valuation, including two Wuxi logistics parks sold to a sponsor-led fund.
Additionally, the
real estate investment trust
(REIT) announced a S$141 million Changi South redevelopment to convert two older assets into a five-storey ramp-up facility, expanding gross floor area by 34% with completion targeted for the second quarter of 2029.
Aggregate leverage dipped to 37.5% from 40.5% because perpetual securities proceeds were temporarily used to repay debt; pro forma gearing would be 40.4%.
Management flags higher-for-longer interest rates and currency volatility as ongoing headwinds.
Related articles:
Is Mapletree Logistics Trust’s 6.8% Distribution Yield Safe?
The Logistics Boom: Why Mapletree Logistics Trust Is a Global Powerhouse
Can Genting’s cash reserve carry the dividend?
Genting Singapore owns and operates Resorts World Sentosa (RWS), one of Singapore’s two integrated resorts.
For the first half of 2026 (1H2026), gaming revenue slipped 0.9% YoY to S$804.4 million.
Non-gaming revenue partly offset this, growing 6.4% to S$398.8 million on the back of a 9% rise in hotel room revenue.
Net profit fell 33.5% to S$156.1 million.
Depreciation and amortisation rose 25% as Genting upgraded its assets, and interest income fell 55% as market rates came down.
Here’s the thing: depreciation doesn’t cost cash.
Operating cash flow gives a clearer picture.
Genting generated S$331.4 million in cash flow from operations during the period.
Capital expenditure, mostly for the multi-year RWS 2.0 expansion, swallowed S$322.5 million, leaving free cash flow at S$8.9 million – an improvement from negative S$5.8 million a year earlier.
The dividend held all the same.
The board declared an interim tax-exempt dividend of S$0.02 per share, unchanged YoY.
Genting’s balance sheet makes that possible.
As at 30 June 2026, the group held S$2.9 billion in cash and had no borrowings, excluding lease liabilities.
Free cash flow is the lifeblood of dividends, and Genting’s is running thin.
RWS 2.0 won’t be finished until 2030.
Until then, the cash reserve carries much of the load.
Management has also flagged geopolitical uncertainty, higher travel costs and softer tourism demand.
Related articles:
Is Genting Singapore Becoming a Better Dividend Stock?
Is Genting Singapore’s Almost 7% Dividend Yield Sustainable?
Will FLCT’s new warehouses pay for the debt behind them?
FLCT owns 114 logistics, industrial and commercial properties across Australia, Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and Singapore, with assets under management of S$7.1 billion.
For context, FLCT reports financials only half-yearly.
Its update for the third quarter of the fiscal year ending 30 September 2026 included no revenue, NPI or DPU figures.
The full-year numbers arrive in November.
The operating numbers have improved.
Portfolio occupancy recovered to 96.1%, up from 92.5% a year ago.
Logistics and industrial (L&I) assets are effectively full at 99.7%, and L&I rental reversion came in at 11.9%.
The commercial side is weaker, with rental reversion at -0.3%.
At Alexandra Technopark, FLCT renewed nine leases at 3.6% below expiring rents, and occupancy dipped to 85.3%.
FLCT is also buying growth.
It acquired interests in four freehold German and Dutch logistics properties for about S$441.5 million.
Management expects the deal to lift DPU by 1.7%.
The catch? FLCT paid for it entirely with debt.
Aggregate leverage rose 1.7 percentage points to 35.4%.
Once the deal settles, aggregate leverage will reach around 38.7% on a pro forma basis, leaving less room below 40%, the level FLCT measures its debt headroom against.
If FLCT issues new units for its next deal, they could eat into that 1.7% gain.
Related articles:
Frasers Property’s Capital Recycling: What It Means for FCT and FLCT
CLI, MLT, FLCT and PLife REIT Earnings: What Investors Should Know Now
Get Smart: Trace the cash before you trust the yield
A yield tells you what a company has paid.
It doesn’t tell you what will pay for the next
dividend
.
Before you buy, check whether this year’s operating cash covers the payout.
If it doesn’t, find out what fills the gap and how long that can last.
FLCT’s full-year results in November are a good place to start.

title: 3 Hidden Gem Stocks to Watch in November
article:
Three smaller
SGX dividend payers
are set to issue their business updates within two weeks of each other this coming November.
Company
Ticker
Business update date
Elite UK REIT
SGX: MXNU
Monday, 2 November 2026
United Overseas Insurance
SGX: U13
Thursday, 5 November 2026
United Hampshire US REIT
SGX: ODBU
Friday, 13 November 2026
These quarterly updates usually carry less detail than full results.
Nevertheless, they can still tell you whether the forces behind each company’s first-half numbers are at work.
Here’s the thing: in all three cases, the first-half headline told only part of the story.
Can Elite UK REIT turn a stronger balance sheet into steady DPU growth?
Elite UK REIT
(SGX: MXNU) owns 148 commercial properties across the UK, valued at £488.8 million on a pro forma basis as at 30 June 2026.
Crucially, UK government tenants occupy more than 99% of the portfolio under long-term triple-net leases.
On the surface, the trust’s first-half performance for 2026 (1H2026) looked flat.
Revenue edged up 0.8% year on year (YoY) to £18.9 million, while distribution per unit (DPU) grew a modest 0.6% to £0.0155.
A year earlier, the REIT booked a one-off dilapidation settlement that inflated the year-ago base.
Strip it out, and adjusted net property income (NPI) grew 5.0% YoY to £18.0 million, while adjusted DPU rose 3.3%.
Management has also taken active steps to de-risk the trust’s balance sheet.
Net gearing fell to 34.6% as at 30 June 2026, from 40.7% at the end of 2025, and 99% of borrowings sit on fixed rates.
In February 2026, a lease regear with the Department for Work and Pensions stretched the weighted average lease expiry to 7.1 years from 2.4 years.
While management expects full-year DPU to rise steadily, it remains cautious given broader
macroeconomic uncertainties
.
On 2 November, watch the next acquisition.
Unitholders have approved the purchase of five government-leased properties for £31.9 million, and proceeds from divestments in Wales will fund £9.3 million of that.
How the manager funds the rest will shape both gearing and DPU.
Also watch Lindsay House in Dundee, a £19.4 million student accommodation conversion due to open in September 2027.
Related articles:
3 Hidden Gem Dividend Stocks to Fund Your Retirement
Beyond Blue Chips: 3 REITs Offering 7%+ Dividend Yields
Will UOI’s underwriting gains outlast a shrinking top line?
United Overseas Insurance Limited (SGX: U13)
, or UOI, is a Singapore-based general insurer within the United Overseas Bank (UOB) group.
Its 1H2026 numbers pulled in opposite directions.
Insurance revenue slipped 8.9% YoY to S$52.1 million.
At the same time, net profit after tax expanded 28.4% to S$11.1 million.
How did that happen?
Management put the softer top line down to timing.
Business grew during the half, but UOI will recognise that revenue in future periods.
Claims also eased.
Lower gross incurred claims reduced overall insurance service expenses to S$37.2 million, lifting the net insurance service and financial result by 37.1% YoY to S$7.0 million.
UOI lifted its interim dividend to S$0.09 per share from S$0.07 earlier, representing a total cash distribution of S$5.5 million.
The group held S$76.3 million in bank balances and fixed deposits as at 30 June 2026 and had no borrowings.
The big question on 5 November is whether revenue recovers as the deferred business flows through. Watch claims too.
Management has flagged claims
inflation
as a risk.
Also note that hedging and favourable currency movements added S$1.1 million to non-underwriting income in the first half.
Those gains may not repeat, so underwriting will need to carry more of the load.
Related articles:
Beyond the STI: 3 Under-the-Radar Dividend Stocks to Watch This May
Beyond Blue Chips: 3 SGX Stocks to Watch in August 2026
Can UHREIT’s acquisitions keep DPU growth ahead of a bigger unit base?
United Hampshire US REIT
(SGX: ODBU), or UHREIT, owns 21 grocery-anchored and necessity-based retail properties in the US, along with two self-storage properties, valued at US$798.5 million.
In 1H2026, gross revenue rose 5.8% YoY to US$37.8 million, while NPI grew 6.4% to US$25.5 million.
Distributable income followed suit, climbing 5.8% to US$13.7 million.
DPU is where the growth thinned out: it rose 3.4% YoY to US$0.0216.
Part of the reason is simple: more units now share the income.
Units in issue rose to 608.2 million from 596.9 million a year earlier, partly through the distribution reinvestment plan and the payment of management fees in units.
Grocery and necessity assets held committed occupancy at 97.6%, and self-storage occupancy rose 430 basis points to 93.5%.
Two recent buys, Dover Marketplace in August 2025 and Wallingford Fair in January 2026, both contributed to the YoY comparison for the first time.
When UHREIT updates on 13 November, watch whether acquisitions and built-in rent escalations can keep distributable income growing faster than the unit count.
Also check that the St Lucie West development, fully pre-leased to Florida Blue for 10 years, stays on track for completion by 1Q2027.
Related articles:
Forget Banks: 3 S-REITs Surprising Unitholders with Higher DPUs
Can These 4 Singapore REITs Pay You S$2,000 Every Month in Retirement?
Get Smart: Read the update against the half-year results
A business update may not hand you a fresh DPU or dividend, but it still gives you enough to test the story.
Before each update, jot down the one driver behind the last set of numbers.
For UHREIT, it’s whether distributable income keeps growing faster than the unit count.
When the update arrives, check which way that driver has moved.
If it moves the right way, the next distribution stands on firmer ground.
If it doesn’t, you’ve got an early warning before the full results arrive.

title: Binance says US$6.3 bil impacted as crypto reels from hack
article:
Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, said US$6.3 billion of funds have been impacted in what the industry is describing as crypto’s biggest ever hack. Digital tokens tumbled.

“The estimated total impact sits at around US$6.3B,” Binance said in a post on X. “We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~US$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.”

Binance has temporarily suspended all deposits and withdrawals. It said it will cover all losses and “user funds are safe.”

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said North Korea was behind the heist, which it called “the largest crypto theft on record.”

“TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s elite hacking unit, based on robust on and off-chain intelligence,” the firm said. “We make this judgment with high confidence.”

Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost US$1.5 billion of tokens. For crypto faithful who’d been basking in a two-month-long price rebound, the Binance incident is a potential setback.

See also: Bitcoin dips below US$80,000 as AI-related market selloff deepens

Notorious previous episodes of theft and fraud among fallen crypto giants such as FTX and Mt. Gox set the stage for protracted bear markets, bruises the industry has worked to put behind it in US President Donald Trump’s promised new era of regulatory clarity for cryptocurrencies.

Bitcoin slumped 3% at the end of the US session and a further 3% in Asia trading, falling below US$77,000 to its lowest level since September, with other tokens also selling off.

“The rumored Binance hack is definitely driving down coin prices,” said Fredrick Collins, chief executive and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data. “Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole, especially as people have already been skittish over the increasing cyber capabilities of AI.”

See also: Bitcoin falls below US$83,000 as AI jitters weigh on sentiment

An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve a backstop for customers in “extreme situations,” according to the exchange. The SAFU is generally maintained at around US$1 billion, but has fluctuated in the past in tandem with market movements, Binance said in 2024.

The two biggest stablecoin issuers said they took steps to freeze missing currency. Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether, said in an X post that it froze more than US$1.5 billion of the stablecoin “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Jeremy Allaire, who runs Circle Internet Group Inc., said US$800 million of its coin had been frozen amid “reports of a potential exploit involving Binance.”

Sentiment was already fragile after a spate of crypto security incidents. In recent months, hundreds of millions of dollars were drained from Bitget, while tampering tied to Ledger devices also led to millions of dollars in losses.

“Attackers are operating at unprecedented speed and scale” but “the tools to track and trace operate at that speed too,” said Ari Redbord, global head of policy at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs. “Stablecoin issuers freeze within hours. Investigators follow funds across chains in real time.”

Traders had already been bracing for greater volatility in the crypto market this week, with US$11 billion in options set to expire Friday. This comes days ahead of the US midterm elections taking place next week, when Democrats could potentially retake one or both chambers of Congress and open the door to greater regulatory scrutiny for the industry.

Exchange thefts and malfeasance have been an ever-present backdrop of crypto’s almost two-decade ascent, the most famous of which was the collapse of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX in November 2022. In what remains perhaps the most notorious hacking incident, Japan-based Bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox was struck in 2011. Over time, the hackers made off with tokens worth billions of dollars based on the current market price. Mt. Gox eventually went bankrupt.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

“It’s a huge damage to crypto because of the consistent successful hacks in the space,” said Tian Zeng, chief executive officer of crypto hedge fund Third Eye. “The fact that exploits keep happening makes it dangerous in the age of newest AI models being released every two weeks.”

The Binance incident came on the same day event-contract venue Polymarket halted trading on its international exchange for an hour after it said that a third-party software provider was compromised. More than 700 Polymarket users were drained of US$2.7 million in funds, said blockchain analytics platform Bubblemaps, in a post on X. A spokesman declined to comment on the numbers.

Recent security incidents haven’t been confined to crypto firms. South Korea’s Daishin Securities disclosed a data leak affecting about 38,000 customers this week, and Mirae Asset Global Investments reported a hacking incident, Yonhap reported. In Japan, hackers on Tuesday threatened to release data of traders using a GMO Internet Group cloud service for foreign-exchange trading.

title: Tuas Power signs MoU to import up to 500 MW of hydropower from Lao PDR
article:
Local power generator Tuas Power has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Électricité du Laos (EDL) and Phongsupthavy Group (PTSG) to explore an arrangement for EDL and PTSG to supply Singapore with up to 500 MW of hydropower from Lao PDR for a term of 5-15 years potentially.

Under the MoU, Tuas Power will import 100 MW in the first contract year, 300 MW in the second and 500MW from the third year onwards. The arrangement potentially provides Tuas Power with renewable hydropower that can be paired to renewable energy certificates (RECS), supplying Singapore with substantial and sustainable energy from the region.

RECs are instruments which verify generation of renewable energy, with each REC representing the non-power, environmental attributes of 1 MWh of renewable energy generated. Under the Oct 27 revised Singapore Standard 673 Code of Practice for Renewable Energy Certificates, RECs must be linked to renewable electricity physically supplied to Singapore’s local power grid. Previously, due to Singapore’s limited renewable energy resources and imports, entities were allowed to procure RECs that were not tied to electricity delivered to Singapore’s grid.

Certification of the associated environmental attributes of RECs will be facilitated by T-RECs Energy and offered to customers as an option.

Tuas Power COO Michael Wong says that the potential collaboration with EDL and PSTG provides Tuas Power with the option to offer customers with immediate bundled renewable energy solutions. “With a ramp up to 500 MW over three years and a term of up to 15 years, this supports our long-term roadmap for customers’ decarbonisation and sustainable regional energy transition to a net zero carbon future,” he adds.

EDL managing director Souksavart Sosouphanh says that his company “welcomes the opportunity” to explore the collaboration with Tuas Power and PSTG. “Regional power trade in ASEAN has made good progress in recent years, and we believe deeper cooperation among likeminded partners can support a more integrated ASEAN Power Grid.”

See also: Sembcorp Industries grows Singapore power portfolio with new power plant; to explore energy solutions with DayOne

PTSG chairman Phongsavath Senaphuan says: “We look forward to working with Tuas Power, an experienced power player in the Singapore market with a strong track record in generation and retail, to explore how our hydropower portfolio can serve Singapore’s growing demand for clean energy. We recognise that hydropower is a seasonal resource, and we will work towards a supply profile that is transparent and deliverable, should the arrangement proceed.”

title: Oil surges on signs US may resume military strikes against Iran
article:
(Oct 20): Oil surged on signs the US may resume military strikes against Iran, risking fresh turbulence in the region that may hurt energy flows.

Brent climbed towards US$118 a barrel, hitting the highest level since April, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) was near US$105. A top commander briefed US President Donald Trump on military options on Thursday, the Wall Street Journal reported. The US leader has repeatedly given signals he may restart airstrikes against Tehran after midterm elections next week.

In Iran, one of the country’s top negotiators, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, suggested that the Islamic Republic’s positions on ending the war would not be compromised. His remarks followed confirmation from Tehran that officials had received a letter sent by US Vice-President JD Vance, which the WSJ reported as a bid to revive the nations’ peace negotiations.

Global benchmark Brent has rallied 14% in October, hitting a six-month high, despite a revival in flows through the Strait of Hormuz, with producers managing to ship cargoes even with elevated risks to shipping. Low inventories and tight supplies of refined products have also supported prices, in part following waves of Ukrainian attacks on Russian processors.

“Even if physical flows recover, traders will find it difficult to keep short positions for long without the US and Iran formally agreeing to a ceasefire,” said Naohiro Niimura, a partner at energy consultancy firm Market Risk Advisory Co, referring to investors holding wagers on lower crude prices.

Regional risks were in focus again as a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while completing an outbound transit of Hormuz on Thursday, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations. Meanwhile, ExxonMobil Holdings Corp and Chevron Corp cancelled plans to attend the ADIPEC oil conference in Abu Dhabi next month amid heightened security concerns.

See also: Bangladesh in talks to buy more American gas, says US ambassador

Away from the Middle East, Ukraine’s military has paused its strikes against Russian oil refineries following pressure from President Trump, the WSJ reported, citing people with knowledge of the operations. The unofficial move began early last week and is expected to last until after the US midterms, potentially extending further into November, it said.
• Brent for December settlement, which expires Friday, added 2.4% to US$117.61 a barrel at 9.52am in Singapore.



See also: Petrobras pumps at record as Iran war upends oil markets

The midterms — which will be held on Nov 3, halfway through Trump’s second term — determine control of Congress. Ahead of the contests, national polls show that the war in Iran is unpopular, with many voters also unhappy about rising living expenses, including fuel costs. Average diesel prices have risen almost 80% this year, hitting a record in September.

In Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies secured 53 seats in the general election held this week, ahead of the main opposition’s bloc of 48 but short of a majority allowing them to rule without further backing. The country joined with the US to start the war against in Iran in late February with the stated aim of dismantling its nuclear programme.

The oil supermajors will wrap up a flood of earnings this week, with results from ExxonMobil and Chevron due later on Friday. Shell plc chief executive officer Wael Sawan said on Thursday that current oil prices no longer looked temporary because global inventories were so depleted.

title: Seatrium secures $200 million contract from SBM Offshore
article:
Mainboard-listed Seatrium has announced it has won a $200 million contract from SBM Offshore for integration works on a floating, production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel.

Seatrium’s scope of work comprises the fabrication of key mooring and riser support structures, flare tower and associated topside support structures, vessel modification and drydocking activities, as well as the integration of topside modules. The scope also includes mechanical completion activities, selected pre-commissioning works, and support for commissioning and sea trials.

Marlin Khiew, executive vice president of Seatrium Energy (Projects) says that the contracts award reinforces Seatrium’s “longstanding” partnership with SBM Offshore. “Leveraging the experience and lessons learned from previous projects, together with our engineering expertise and established track record of delivery with certainty, we are proud to support South America's offshore development and its growing role in global energy supply, contributing to greater energy security and long-term economic growth," adds Khiew, who is also Seatrium’s president of LATAM.

Project execution is expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026, with completion scheduled for 2029.

Shares in Seatrium are down one cent, or 0.5%, to $1.83 as at around 10.20 am on Oct 30.

title: Bangladesh in talks to buy more American gas, says US ambassador
article:
(Oct 30): Bangladesh is poised to sign deals to buy more US liquefied natural gas (LNG) as the Trump administration pushes to expand energy exports, says the American ambassador to the country.

Several LNG sales proposals are in various stages of the approval process with the Bangladeshi government, and agreements to buy liquefied petroleum gas could follow, said Ambassador Brent Christensen.

“We think there are going to be several more deals signed soon,” he said in an interview in Dhaka. “We want to make sure that our allies and partners have reliable sources of energy.”

Bangladesh is grappling with a fuel shortfall as the Middle East war has choked LNG shipments from Qatar, the country’s main supplier, behind the Strait of Hormuz. The disruption has forced countries across Asia to seek alternatives, and the US — already the world’s largest exporter of natural gas — is positioning itself to replace lost shipments.

The US estimates Bangladesh’s LNG market could be worth about US$10 billion next year, and it could potentially grow to US$30 billion by 2050, Christensen said. The country’s previous government failed to develop enough new domestic gas supply to offset declining output from older fields, forcing the country to become more reliant on expensive overseas LNG.

Washington and Dhaka signed an energy cooperation memorandum in May that created a framework for US companies to participate in government-to-government procurement of LNG and other types of energy. The pact is part of the White House’s broader push to use commercial diplomacy to boost American exports.

See also: Petrobras pumps at record as Iran war upends oil markets

The US-based unit of Centalion Group Ltd — the trading house formerly known as Gunvor — used the framework to cement a deal to sell American LNG to Bangladesh for more than a decade starting this year.

Chevron Corp, the biggest gas producer in the South Asian nation, is looking to expand, Christensen said.

“Continued domestic gas exploration and production can strengthen energy security, support growth and reduce exposure to market volatility,” Shu Xiong, president and managing director of Chevron Bangladesh, said in an emailed response to questions. “Chevron has supported Bangladesh’s energy development for more than three decades and looks forward to helping power its next chapter.”

See also: Oil jumps with Israeli election and Iran attack report in focus

Energy-equipment provider GE Vernova Inc is also keen to do more business in Bangladesh, Christensen said. GE Vernova didn’t respond to a request for comment.

Beyond natural gas, Christensen said that US developers of small modular nuclear reactors are interested in having discussions with Bangladeshi officials about potential projects.

“We are very active in supporting our companies and identifying opportunities for them and helping them resolve longstanding business issues here,” he said. “No other administration has put anywhere close to this priority on commercial diplomacy.”

title: Stock sell-off deepens on tech earnings, bonds rise
article:
(Oct 30): Technology shares led a global stock sell-off as another round of disappointing earnings accelerated a rotation out of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade and drove investors towards haven assets such as Treasuries. Crude oil rallied.

Futures for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index slid 2.3% after earnings from Amazon.com Inc and Intel Corp underwhelmed and raised fresh concerns about spending on the rollout of the AI technology. Bitcoin fell almost 3% to around US$76,600 after Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, suspended all deposits and withdrawals as it investigated a suspected hack.

The Kospi Index — a key barometer of the global AI trade — dropped over 5%, set for its biggest one-day drop in two weeks. Chip heavyweights sold off, dragging the broader MSCI Asia Pacific Index down 1.6%. While tech was the biggest loser, five of the gauge’s 11 subgroups advanced as traders continued to rotate out of the hottest trade of the year. Amazon slumped 7.3% in extended trading, while Intel plunged 23%.

“This earnings season has been tough on AI players, with most getting punished against a backdrop of AI-bubble and inflation fears,” said Anna Wu, an investment strategist and founder of Floodlines Research. “The concern isn’t that AI demand has already slowed. It’s that higher funding costs and credit risk could eventually force hyperscalers to slow their build-out.”

As sentiment worsened, traders sought safety in haven assets such as the Swiss franc, the yen and Treasuries. The Swiss and the Japanese currencies were among the biggest gainers against the dollar among Group-of-10 peers, while US government debt rallied across the curve.

After a three-day rally this week, technology stocks lost momentum on Thursday as Samsung’s earnings fell short of investor expectations and Alphabet Inc posted a record drop following its results announcement.

See also: Tech stocks drop as Alphabet, Samsung disappoint

The latest earnings have deepened doubts over the AI trade, raising questions about whether heavy spending can generate returns quickly enough to justify lofty valuations. Even so, the damage has largely been confined to tech, with more than 400 S&P 500 Index members advancing Thursday as investors rotated into more defensive stocks and haven assets.

Chip stocks were among the hardest hit Thursday, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling 1.4%. The Nasdaq 100 gauge dropped 1.4% and the S&P 500 Index retreated 0.3%. Microsoft Corp, though, drew blowout demand for its US$25 billion ($32 billion) debt offering.

“The broader message is that investors want more than AI promises,” said Greg Boland, a market strategist at broker Moomoo. “With technology valuations stretched, the market is demanding clearer evidence that heavy investment will deliver profits and cash flow, driving risk-off sentiment across tech stocks and spilling into Asian markets.”

See also: Asian stocks rise, Treasuries steady before Fed decision

Meanwhile, the yen gained 0.2% to 157.45 per dollar ahead of the Bank of Japan’s interest rate decision.

The central bank is widely expected to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged on Friday while indicating that underlying inflation has finally reached its 2% target.

Elsewhere, oil rose on signs the US may resume military strikes against Iran, risking fresh turbulence in the region that may hurt energy flows. Brent advanced above US$117 a barrel after swinging more than US$3 in the previous session.

US Treasuries extended their gains from Thursday, when they rallied across the curve as a hedge against a potential economic slowdown. Shorter-dated debt led the advance as traders priced in slightly reduced odds of rate increases by the Federal Reserve in the coming months.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury fell two basis points to 4.92% in Asian trading.

The bond rally came even as US data pointed to a resilient economy and persistent price pressures. A day after the Fed kept rates steady, figures showed the economy expanded in the third quarter at the fastest pace in a year, while the personal consumption expenditures price index — the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge — rose 0.5% in September, the most in six months.

“It was another strong round of economic data that shows ongoing inflationary pressures and growth split between the AI buildout and consumption,” said Ian Lyngen at BMO Capital Markets.

Some of the main moves in markets:
• The Japanese yen rose 0.1% to 157.50 per dollar
• The offshore yuan was little changed at 6.6560 per dollar
• The Australian dollar was little changed at US$0.7035
• The yield on 10-year Treasuries declined two basis points to 4.92%

title: Nvidia CEO says ties to Singapore company under spying probe were ‘normal’
article:
(Oct 30): Nvidia Corp chief executive officer Jensen Huang said the chipmaker’s dealings with Megaspeed International were “normal and not unusual” following a New York Times report that one of the Singapore firm’s executives is under investigation for spying on behalf of China.

Nvidia’s relationship with Megaspeed’s officials was proper, and the chipmaker has checked to ensure that Megaspeed didn’t illegally send its artificial intelligence (AI) processors to China, Huang said in an interview Thursday. That country is barred from buying Nvidia’s powerful AI chips — known as graphics processing units, or GPUs — under US export rules.

“We’ve studied all their deployments of our GPUs and counted every one,” he said in the interview. “And I think the US government also has as well.”

The remarks follow a Times story that the US government is investigating an executive from Megaspeed for allegedly providing information to the Chinese government. Huang Le has previously been pictured with Nvidia’s leader on social media, and the story reports that she may have been serving as a Chinese agent aiming to evade chip export controls.

In the interview, Huang said that his interactions with her were typical of those with Chinese customers and executives. She’s no longer with Megaspeed, he said.

“Our relationship, our interactions, have been related to Megaspeed, and it was all completely normal and not unusual,” Huang said. The CEO said he hadn’t been informed by the US government of its suspicions about Huang Le.

See also: Singtel’s NCS new AI Mission Centre to move trials into daily operations

The growing geopolitical rivalry between the US and China has led to increasing clampdowns by Washington on exports of key American technology. That’s cut off Nvidia from a lucrative source of revenue in China, the largest market for chips.

The company has received some latitude to ship a limited amount of older AI-related products to the Asian country under the Trump administration. That approval hasn’t resulted in a material amount of shipments, at least in part because Beijing has sought to limit the deliveries itself in an effort to foster its own chip industry.

Nonetheless, the restrictions on exports have led to investigations and charges of smuggling of Nvidia’s best products to China — something the company has said is an insignificant issue. Megaspeed is one of a group of companies that Bloomberg News and others have reported may have tried to illegally divert shipments of chips intended for data centres outside of China into that country.

title: Indonesia rain set to ease toxic haze in Singapore, Malaysia
article:
(Oct 29): Indonesia is set for more consistent rain next month, providing relief from wildfires that have spewed toxic smoke across Singapore and Malaysia, though widespread downpours are still weeks away.

Rainfall has picked up across Indonesia in recent days, helping to replenish soil moisture after months of severe drought triggered by El Niño, according to weather data. While that’s offered some respite, heavier rain isn’t expected until at least early December in regions such as Kalimantan, where blazes have raged and most of the remaining fire hotspots are located.

The choking haze from Indonesia’s worst fire season in years has cloaked local towns and drifted across neighbouring countries for weeks, closing schools, driving demand for air purifiers and straining diplomatic ties. Singapore’s foreign minister visited Jakarta this week to ease widening tensions, with the two countries agreeing to establish a joint taskforce on forest fires.

Indonesia has received less than a quarter of its normal rainfall since June, according to Atmospheric G2, leaving the landscape bone-dry and making fires often linked to slash-and-burn agricultural practices harder to contain. Nearly 13,500 hotspots have been detected nationwide so far this month, the most since 2015, and adding to high counts in September and August, the forestry ministry’s SiPongi platform shows.

“Substantial rainfall should fall through November, generally increasing further in December and remaining significant into early 2027,” said Andreas Vallgren, chief science officer at weather intelligence firm Ignitia. “Whether this is sufficient to extinguish existing fires, particularly in peatlands, will depend on how consistently rainfall reaches the affected areas.”

See also: RegCo issues additional queries to SGX-listed companies with links to haze

Over recent weeks, Kuala Lumpur and Singapore have frequently topped the rankings of the world’s most polluted cities, according to data from IQAir. The city-state has flagged possible legal action against companies suspected of illegal burning, while more than 1,000 people protested in central Jakarta on Wednesday over the government’s handling of the fires.

Indonesia’s agricultural activity has been impacted. Smog from the wildfires is impairing the activity of weevils that pollinate oil palms in the world’s biggest grower, while haze is slowing harvesting at estates owned by major producer SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG) in Kalimantan and Sumatra, and could weigh on productivity.

The combination of fires and dry weather has prompted the Indonesian Palm Oil Association to trim its production estimates for next year to 56.6 million tonnes, a two-year low, according to M Hadi Sugeng Wahyudiono, secretary general of the industry group. That compares with an earlier forecast of 59 million tonnes.

See also: Singapore expands haze inquiries to 10 locally based firms

Still, forecasts point to improving conditions. Near-normal rainfall is expected next month, helping to prevent new fires from developing and curb the spread of existing blazes, according to weather forecasting startup Plannette AI. “Rains will ease fires in Borneo and Sumatra” by December, said chief executive officer and founder Hansi Singh.

Indonesian authorities are hopeful the fire crisis can be resolved in November, said Budi Harsoyo, a senior official at the country’s national weather agency, known as BMKG. Satellite monitoring suggests that the development of hotspots in three provinces hit hardest by fires may be letting up, he added.

There are rising chances of monthly rainfall exceeding 300mm in parts of South Sumatra, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan in December, BMKG said this week. Precipitation is expected to pick up in the first week of the month, according to an outlook from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts.

One wildcard risk, said Ignitia’s Vallgren, is that the persistence of fires and smoke can crimp rainfall, because the smog blocks sunrays and inhibits the convective process that forms storms and showers.

History offers a cautionary tale. In 1997, blazes that burned and grew during the prolonged dry season that year were briefly suppressed when rains finally arrived in December, weeks later than normal, but reignited in early 1998 as the rainy season ended prematurely due to a lingering El Niño.

“There is a feedback loop — more fires mean more smoke, which can act to suppress rainfall, which in turn can delay rainfall,” Vallgren said. On the other hand, “if some strong rainfall events make it, they do help to clean the air to some degree, which helps kick-start more frequent storms”.

title: US stock rotation hits AI winners on spending worries
article:
(Oct 30): A selloff in several tech companies spurred a rotation into a broader category of stocks while fueling a push toward the safety of bonds.

The record plunge in Alphabet Inc shares on disappointing sales revived doubts over the artificial-intelligence trade. The Nasdaq 100 lost 1.4%. Microsoft Corp drew blowout demand for its US$25 billion debt offering. In late hours, Amazon.com Inc slumped as its spending soared on efforts to meet demand for AI services. Intel Corp.’s revenue forecast missed estimates.

Not every tech firm fell, but a basket of AI winners sank 2.7%. In a sign of rotation, over 400 shares in the S&P 500 rose.

Thursday’s price action was a “microcosm” of what the stock market has experienced for much of October: Concerns about the AI trade weighing on technology and communication services, but leaving other areas relatively unscathed, said Chris Larkin at E*Trade from Morgan Stanley.

Tech losses revived the haven appeal of Treasuries, with short-dated notes outperforming. Oil wavered as traders parsed conflicting signals on the direction of US military strategy in Iran.

Just a day after the Federal Reserve left rates steady, data showed the US economy expanded in the third quarter at the fastest pace in a year. Meanwhile, the personal consumption expenditures price index — the Fed’s preferred inflation measure — rose 0.5% in September, the most in six months.

See also: Tech stocks slide as Alphabet’s record plunge revives AI fears

“It was another strong round of economic data that shows ongoing inflationary pressures and growth split between the AI buildout and consumption,” said Ian Lyngen at BMO Capital Markets.

AI is still the major theme for activity, but economic resilience is still a broad-based story, according to Eli Nir and Oscar Munoz at TD Securities.

“Couple that with the AI-led inflationary pressures, and it’s clear why the Fed both upgraded its growth assessment and remained acutely focused on their inflation mandate,” they added.

See also: Pimco offloads billions in AI debt just in time to skirt losses — Bloomberg

White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett hinted that he expected the Fed would raise rates if inflation figures for this month are elevated.

“If October comes out really high, then I think the Fed would probably appropriately act,” he told Bloomberg Television.

Elsewhere, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde played down the danger that inflation will spread beyond energy after news that she’ll step down early overshadowed a decision to leave rates untouched.

title: Tech stocks slide as Alphabet’s record plunge revives AI fears
article:
(Oct 30): Tech stocks were dragged lower by a record drop in Alphabet Inc after disappointing results renewed investor concerns about the threat that artificial intelligence (AI) poses to its core business.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index was down 1.4% as of 12.15pm in New York, while the S&P 500 fell 0.4%. Stocks outside the tech sector were broadly higher, with around 390 stocks in the benchmark index gaining while the S&P 500 Equal Weight Index advanced 0.9%.

Alphabet shares fell 10%, setting the stock up for its biggest-ever market value wipeout, after the company reported disappointing search and advertising sales that reinforced worries about AI’s threat to its core business.

“After missing forecasts on essentially every key metric except cloud revenue tonight, Google is playing the AI Hunger Games from a position of weakness,” Michael O’Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading Institutional Services LLC, wrote in a note on Wednesday. “Disappointing results in advertising, a business it and Meta Platforms dominate globally, illustrate the key risk investors fear.”

The latest earnings have renewed doubts over the AI trade, raising questions about whether significant spending on the technology can generate returns quickly enough to justify lofty valuations. Investors will get even more earnings to parse when Amazon.com Inc reports after the market closes on Thursday.

Chip stocks took a hit, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling 1%. Software shares were also lower on Thursday after disappointing quarterly results from ServiceNow Inc and Fortinet Inc added to the broader concerns. The companies’ shares traded down by 26% and 21%, respectively.

See also: Pimco offloads billions in AI debt just in time to skirt losses — Bloomberg

Investors were slightly more encouraged by Microsoft Corp, which reported earnings after the close on Wednesday. The company posted surging growth in its cloud business while keeping its capital expenditures in check. Shares fell 1.3% on Thursday.

Meanwhile Caterpillar Inc, which builds power-generation equipment used for data centres, saw its shares slump 8.1% after posting third-quarter earnings that only modestly beat expectations.

Outside of AI, DoorDash Inc shares gained 4.5% after the company reported earnings that beat estimates and announced its US$17 billion deal to buy Instacart.

See also: S&P 500 churns in countdown to Fed, tech earnings

Stocks ended the day higher on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve voted to hold interest rates steady.
• Cruise stocks like Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd and Carnival Corp gained after Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd raised its full-year guidance in a sign that turnaround efforts are taking hold. The stock jumped 10%.
• Payment stocks are gaining after Mastercard Inc reported better-than-anticipated earnings due to more spending from US consumers.
